Finite-shot optimization and independent readout

The first optimization examples fit angles using exact statevector expectations and sample only the final readout. This increment instead makes each parameter decision from finite outcomes. It uses the same four-vertex MaxCut cycle, the same two-qubit Hamiltonian H=−Z0−Z1+12X0X1H=-Z_0-Z_1+\tfrac12X_0X_1H=−Z0​−Z1​+21​X0​X1​, and the same explicit QAOA and VQE circuits Farhi et al., 2014Peruzzo et al., 2014.

Scope of the experiment

These are reproducible ideal finite-shot simulations. Counts are drawn classically from explicit circuit statevector probabilities; they are not hardware measurements. Training uses the sampled objectives and their descriptive standard errors. Exact diagnostics and fresh final readout are reported separately and do not choose the training moves.

The finite schedule and acceptance rule are heuristics. The observed trajectories do not certify convergence, optimal angles, or a success probability for the optimizer. The original fixed-readout projection concerns the final readout only; the later sections separately cost complete stored trajectories and the size-study workloads. The complete recorded-trajectory replay maps training and holdout batches as fixed circuit inputs. Predicting the cost of a new hardware-driven adaptive path remains planned.

Tasks, targets, and predetermined runs¶

For QAOA, maximize expected cut on edges (0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(0,3)(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(0,3)(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(0,3) by minimizing fQ=−⟨C⟩f_Q=-\langle C\ranglefQ​=−⟨C⟩. For VQE, minimize fV=⟨H⟩f_V=\langle H\ranglefV​=⟨H⟩. QAOA uses one layer with phase CX; RZ(-gamma); CX per edge and mixer RX(2*beta). VQE uses RY(theta) on qubit zero followed by CX(0,1). All angles are radians. Input preparation, phase operations, mixer, basis changes, and measurement are explicit in the circuits.

These three seed/start pairs are declared before running either task. Seed 7 is the primary example and the input to the fixed-readout resource projection; no run is chosen after comparing outcomes. The requested toy quality targets are final exact expected cut at least 2.90 and final exact VQE energy gap at most 0.03 above E0=−17/2E_0=-\sqrt{17}/2E0​=−17​/2. They are evaluated after training with independent analytic and matrix references. They do not stop the optimizer, certify finite-shot confidence, or impose an angle-accuracy requirement.

These runs optimize sampled objectives. Ideal measurement outcomes are generated from statevector probabilities; exact expectations are used only for post-decision diagnostics. They are modeled ideal measurements, rather than executed hardware shots.

The bounded schedule contains four blocks of eight sweeps: (step radians, shots/group) = (0.4, 256), (0.2, 512), (0.1, 1024), (0.05, 2048). The initial objective uses 256 shots/group. Each sweep freshly measures its incumbent and both coordinate proposals for every parameter, including all rejected proposals. A candidate is accepted only when the sampled decrease exceeds twice the combined estimated standard error; this margin is a heuristic, without a confidence or convergence guarantee across adaptive choices. Every run stops after the prescribed 32 sweeps.

Each seed is paired with a different fixed initialization. These six cases jointly vary initialization and measurement randomness; they do not isolate the two effects. Fresh validation uses 4,096 shots per group and a separate keyed random-stream family after training ends.

What one sampled objective contains¶

QAOA uses one all-Z group. Each bitstring yields its complete cut size C(z)C(z)C(z), sharing the outcomes across all four edges. The minimized estimate is f^Q=−C‾\widehat f_Q=-\overline Cf​Q​=−C. Its descriptive standard error is sQ=Var^(C)/Ns_Q=\sqrt{\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(C)/N}sQ​=Var(C)/N​, using sample variance of whole cut scores.

VQE uses two independently sampled groups. All-Z outcomes score YZ=−Z0−Z1∈[−2,2]Y_Z=-Z_0-Z_1\in[-2,2]YZ​=−Z0​−Z1​∈[−2,2]. All-X outcomes, obtained by H basis changes on both qubits, score YX=12X0X1∈[−1/2,1/2]Y_X=\tfrac12X_0X_1\in[-1/2,1/2]YX​=21​X0​X1​∈[−1/2,1/2]. Then

f^V=Y‾Z+Y‾X,sV=Var^(YZ)NZ+Var^(YX)NX.\widehat f_V=\overline Y_Z+\overline Y_X,\qquad s_V=\sqrt{\frac{\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(Y_Z)}{N_Z} +\frac{\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(Y_X)}{N_X}}.f​V​=YZ​+YX​,sV​=NZ​Var(YZ​)​+NX​Var(YX​)​​.
(1)

The two Z terms are scored jointly from the same bitstrings, so their covariance is retained. They are not treated as independent term measurements. Every VQE objective call uses the stated shot count in each of its two groups. No symmetry filtering, error mitigation, device noise, or extra postselection is applied.

A fixed, fully recorded training schedule¶

The sampled polling optimizer makes one initial objective call at 256 shots per group. It then runs 32 sweeps in four blocks. Each block uses its stated step and shot count for all eight sweeps; lack of an accepted move does not alter the schedule.

SweepsCoordinate displacement, radiansShots per group per call
1–80.4256
9–160.2512
17–240.11,024
25–320.052,048

Every sweep remeasures the incumbent at that sweep’s shot count, then evaluates both negative and positive displacements along each coordinate from that same incumbent. QAOA therefore uses five objective calls per sweep: one incumbent and four proposals. VQE uses three: one incumbent and two proposals. Angles are reduced modulo 2π2\pi2π.

Let f^i,si\widehat f_i,s_if​i​,si​ denote the new incumbent estimate and standard error, and let f^c,sc\widehat f_c,s_cf​c​,sc​ denote the best sampled proposal. A move requires

f^i−f^c>2si2+sc2.\widehat f_i-\widehat f_c>2\sqrt{s_i^2+s_c^2}.f​i​−f​c​>2si2​+sc2​​.
(2)

Otherwise the parameters stay at the incumbent. The run stops when the schedule is exhausted. The combined standard error is descriptive: the rule is not a calibrated hypothesis test or a 95% acceptance guarantee. Selecting among proposals, repeating adaptive comparisons, and occasionally obtaining zero empirical variance prevent that interpretation. An accepted sampled improvement can be an exact deterioration, and a rejected move can be an exact improvement.

NumPy SeedSequence separates random streams with entropy [master_seed, algorithm_id] and spawn keys (family, evaluation_index, group_index) NumPy Developers, n.d.. Algorithm IDs are zero for QAOA and one for VQE; family zero is training and family one is fresh final validation. Keys distinguish calls and measurement groups. They support reproducibility and avoid accidental stream reuse; they do not mathematically prove independence of a pseudorandom generator. The statistical statements here use the ideal independent-sampling model.

The training record retains every sampled call, candidate parameters, group counts, group means, standard errors, stream identifiers, accepted and rejected moves, stopping reason, classical optimizer time, and post-training diagnostics. No exact expectation or analytic derivative enters the acceptance rule.

The plotted exact cut or energy along a trajectory is a diagnostic, rather than an objective available to the sampled optimizer. The exact optimizer from the first increment remains an independent reference. Three predetermined trajectories show behavior on these instances; the fraction meeting a target is not a certified population success probability.

Fresh final readout and what its intervals mean¶

After training, each selected final state receives a fresh 4,096-shot all-Z QAOA readout or fresh 4,096-shot-per-group VQE readout. Validation streams are distinct from all training streams. Exact expectation, sampled estimate, descriptive standard error, and a conservative bounded-score interval are reported separately.

Hoeffding’s inequality bounds independent bounded samples without a normal approximation Hoeffding, 1963. For one final QAOA holdout with NNN scores in [0,4][0,4][0,4], a two-sided interval of failure probability at most δ\deltaδ has radius

ϵQ=4log⁡(2/δ)2N.\epsilon_Q=4\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2N}}.ϵQ​=42Nlog(2/δ)​​.
(3)

For the sum of the independently sampled VQE group means, the group score ranges are four and one. A direct bound for the sum has radius

ϵV=12(16NZ+1NX)log⁡(2/δ).\epsilon_V=\sqrt{\frac12\left(\frac{16}{N_Z}+\frac1{N_X}\right) \log(2/\delta)}.ϵV​=21​(NZ​16​+NX​1​)log(2/δ)​.
(4)

At 4,096 shots per group and δ=0.05\delta=0.05δ=0.05, these radii are about 0.0849 in cut units and 0.0875 in energy units. They refer to one holdout’s expectation estimate. Six individually 95% intervals do not provide a simultaneous 95% statement for all runs. The VQE formula already bounds the combined Z/X estimate; it does not need an additional group split for this statistical interval.

Fresh holdout coverage remains valid conditional on the training history and selected angles under the independent-sampling model. It bounds readout error at those angles. It does not prove that training achieved a target, bound the optimizer’s failure probability, or turn the observed mean into certified optimal angles. In particular, a holdout interval can be too wide to certify the requested 0.03 VQE energy gap even when the toy’s exact diagnostic meets it. Sampled energy can also fall below the exact ground energy through readout noise.

Source:
Finite-shot QAOA and VQE optimization

End-to-end resource analysis¶

All proposals and all incumbent remeasurements count, including rejected moves and the initial call. With the default schedule, one QAOA run has 161 objective calls and 153,856 training shots. One VQE run has 97 objective calls, each with two groups, and 184,832 training shots. These totals follow from the executed trace, rather than from the number of accepted updates.

Workload for the three predetermined runsQAOA shotsVQE shotsTotal shots
Training461,568554,4961,016,064
Fresh final holdout12,28824,57636,864
Training plus holdout473,856579,0721,052,928

Each shot represents a new state preparation in the ideal circuit protocol. The implementation draws counts classically from circuit probabilities, so these are protocol shot counts rather than physical circuit executions. The sampled resource ledger weights the actual circuit gates by every call’s shot count, separates training from validation, includes basis changes and qubit readout, and records unsynthesized rotations. A single final ansatz evaluation is not this hybrid run.

CPU timings measure the local simulator, random sampling, and classical control. They do not measure a quantum device’s reset, routing, gate, measurement, communication, or feedback latency. Input parsing and separate classical reference timing are disclosed where unmeasured. The exact diagnostics and figure-generation work are additional classical checks rather than hidden quantum objective evaluations. The recorded-trajectory replay accounts for this fixed training record; it does not predict a fresh hardware-driven adaptive execution.

Conditional resources for a fixed final readout¶

The projection takes seed 7’s fitted final angles as fixed classical inputs. It estimates only 4,096 QAOA all-Z executions and, separately, 4,096 VQE all-Z plus 4,096 VQE all-X executions. It includes the explicit preparations, rotations, basis changes, and readout of those exported circuits. The sampled training decisions and their million-shot workload are excluded from this physical projection.

Two frozen physical error scenarios, 10-3 and 10-4, use the existing baseline’s 100 ns gate and 500 ns measurement timing assumptions. The declared physical-fault budget is 10-3 for the whole QAOA fixed-readout task and separately 10-3 for VQE’s fixed-readout task; VQE allocates half to each measurement group. That is a physical-fault budget, distinct from the holdout interval’s sampling failure probability and from rotation approximation.

The projections use the pinned Microsoft QDK local resource estimator 1.34.0, released under MIT Microsoft Quantum Development Kit contributors, n.d.. The linked audited source commit is a code pointer, not a claimed package release commit. The native PSSPC rotation model uses a mean empirical fit associated with mixed-fallback gate approximation Kliuchnikov et al., 2022.

Each measured circuit has a per-execution synthesis-model allowance 10-5 with its recorded allocation/count assumptions. It is a conditional expected-cost model, rather than an executed Clifford+T synthesis or a certificate of the resulting cut or energy error. Fitted mean quality does not certify angle accuracy, optimizer success, or convergence. The projection record must be read with those limits and its exact circuit and estimator provenance.

These are conditional mean-fit resource projections for the first predeclared case’s fixed final readout. They exclude all finite-shot optimizer training calls and are not QPU measurements, certified angle syntheses, worst-case bounds, convergence guarantees, or guaranteed observable accuracy.

The profiles use the frozen physical assumptions: error rates 10-3 and 10-4, 100 ns gate time and 500 ns measurement time. Each circuit has 4,096 modeled serial executions. The QAOA task receives physical-fault allowance 10-3; the VQE task receives 10-3 split equally between its Z and X groups. Each circuit separately receives synthesis-model scalar allowance 10-5 per execution.

Reproduce and inspect¶

Use the pinned Python 3.12 environment and the original Qiskit core, NumPy, and Matplotlib packages credited in the parent chapter. No optimizer package or new dependency is required.

python scripts/generate_optimization_sampled.py
python scripts/generate_optimization_projections.py
python scripts/execute_notebooks.py

The physical-projection command requires a source checkout containing the shared src/openquantum/resource_estimation.py adapter and the audited QDK environment. A standalone export of that physical adapter remains planned. The sampled generator and notebook can be reproduced separately from the public downloads below.

The sampled notebook runs the bounded experiment and supplies the labeled figures reused above. Saved outputs serve the static site without a live kernel. To reproduce its public downloads, save the matching standalone module and generator together with the implementation license, using the pinned environment linked by the parent chapter. The generators and records define materialization and simulation limits; no larger-instance convergence behavior is inferred from these examples.

Complete recorded-trajectory resources¶

The fixed final-readout projection omits sampled training. This report instead maps every measured group in the original four-vertex-cycle QAOA and first two-qubit VQE records, including rejected proposals, incumbent remeasurements, initial calls, and fresh final validation. It treats the stored angles and shot allocations as fixed inputs to a recorded-trajectory replay.

What is estimated

Replay means preparing the recorded circuits with their recorded repetitions. Fresh hardware measurements are not allowed to choose different parameters in this cost calculation. A hardware-driven optimizer could follow a different angle path, with different synthesis costs and achieved quality, even when its call and shot schedule is fixed.

The circuit mapping and conditional estimator results have separate status in the generated summary below. A checked mapping is not an executed fault-tolerant run. Physical results use an expected synthesis-cost model; they certify neither concrete synthesized sequences nor worst-case work, runtime tails, convergence, or output-error confidence.

From every sampled batch to an explicit circuit¶

The manifest binds the replay to the source run record, generator, environment, and implementation. The execution mapping identifies the task, run, seed, training or validation phase, call, measurement group, parameters, and shot repetitions for every batch.

Each batch has source and lowered measured OpenQASM files identified by SHA-256. QAOA includes H preparation, edge phases, and mixer rotations. VQE includes its RY/CX preparation and the all-X H basis changes where required. Final qubit-to-classical measurement maps are retained. Initial all-zero availability is an assumption; physical reset time is excluded where unmeasured.

For every batch, the small-system check compares source and lowered unitary operators up to a global phase before final measurement, and verifies the final measurement map separately. That check validates numerical lowering of each particular circuit. It does not validate an approximate Clifford+T replacement of its arbitrary angles.

Identical QASM content can share a stored file by its exact hash. Every original batch still has an execution-mapping entry and its own repetition weight. Exact file deduplication therefore reduces artifact duplication without removing objective evaluations or shots.

Share estimator work only when the native cost model agrees¶

Different fitted angles generally produce different unitaries. Resource-model grouping makes no claim that those unitaries are equivalent. Equal gate counts alone also do not establish equal cost: native trace ordering, repetitions, properties, and resource requirements can affect the estimator.

The model-signature record groups batches after comparing cost-canonical native and PSSPC trace JSON, with the recorded derived metadata. Complete instrumented trace JSON is retained. The cost signature excludes only native EVALUATION_TIME instrumentation, property 7, whose recorded pinned-source audit establishes that it is not consumed by the physical cost calculation. All other fields and properties remain in the comparison. This CPU instrumentation time is not quantum runtime.

The grouping uses the same synthesis setting, physical profile, and per-execution budget. Its equality is equality of inputs relevant to this pinned cost model, rather than equality of circuit behavior at different angles. A bounded second-QASM probe for a shared model class is recorded separately, comparing actual physical Pareto fields under the same budget and profile. Its scope and result are retained rather than treated as a general circuit-equivalence proof.

QDK’s default OpenQASM importer constructs a canonical trace from logical counts, already abstracting continuous angles and original Clifford topology. Comparing those native traces checks equality of inputs inside the declared estimator model; it does not certify a routed schedule for every original gate. The source and lowered QASM, gate counts, measurement maps, and numerical lowering checks preserve the original circuit evidence separately.

Each group retains a representative input and maps all constituent batches to the corresponding estimator report. Their repetition weights are summed only after the model-signature comparison. The projection reports retain the actual estimator outputs and model provenance. The distinction between source-circuit equivalence checks and cost-model grouping is essential: neither substitutes for the other.

Keep physical faults and rotation approximation separate¶

The replay declares a whole-task physical-fault allowance of δQ=10−3\delta_Q=10^{-3}δQ​=10−3 for all 473,856 QAOA shots and, separately, δV=10−3\delta_V=10^{-3}δV​=10−3 for all 579,072 VQE shots. Each task allocates a uniform per-execution allowance,

δα,execution=10−3Nα,α∈{Q,V}.\delta_{\alpha,\mathrm{execution}}= \frac{10^{-3}}{N_\alpha},\qquad \alpha\in\{Q,V\}.δα,execution​=Nα​10−3​,α∈{Q,V}.
(5)

The report checks this allocation across all batches. A union-bound interpretation requires the estimator’s per-execution physical contribution to be a calibrated upper bound for the hardware/model assumptions; the replay does not supply that experimental calibration. Independence of physical faults is not needed for the union bound.

Each prepared circuit also receives a per-execution synthesis-model allowance of 10-5. This is a coherent approximation-model quantity, not a stochastic failure probability. It is not multiplied by the million-shot total and labeled whole-run failure. Each shot prepares a fresh state; repeated preparations do not form one long coherent computation on a shared state. Repetition also does not remove systematic observable bias from an approximate circuit. Adaptive classical feedback can turn changed outcomes into a different parameter path; no approximation or accuracy bound for that complete classical–quantum process is established here.

The pinned Microsoft QDK resource estimator 1.34.0 and native PSSPC model use the audited expected rotation-cost fit Microsoft Quantum Development Kit contributors, n.d.Kliuchnikov et al., 2022. The fit is not an executed synthesis sequence, an instance-specific approximation certificate, a worst-case cost bound, or a bound on fallback-protocol runtime tails. The 10-5 model allowance consequently does not certify the final cut value or energy error. Sampling uncertainty, fitted quality, and physical-fault allocation remain separate quantities.

The two physical profiles retain the frozen 10-3 and 10-4 physical error rates, 100 ns gate time, and 500 ns measurement time. The Grover baseline remains unchanged. This report does not alter requested problem quality or hardware assumptions to manufacture an improvement.

Aggregate serial time and peak footprint with explicit exclusions¶

For a declared model-point selection, serial quantum time is weighted by every batch’s shot count and peak footprint is the maximum selected footprint:

Tserial=∑bNb tb,Qpeak=max⁡bqb.T_{\mathrm{serial}}=\sum_b N_b\,t_b,\qquad Q_{\mathrm{peak}}=\max_b q_b.Tserial​=b∑​Nb​tb​,Qpeak​=bmax​qb​.
(6)

The declared choices can select independent per-model-signature Pareto points. Configuration changes, transport, communication, routing, physical reset, and feedback overhead are excluded where unmeasured. A single common physical layout or factory configuration for the complete trajectory is not certified. Thus these aggregate choices are conditional serial model costs, rather than a measured machine schedule or a globally optimized architecture.

The local CPU-control and objective-simulation timings from the original experiment are reported separately. A simulator’s control time is not a measurement of classical feedback latency in a fault-tolerant processor, and it is not silently added to or hidden inside quantum runtime. Concurrent execution, reuse across shots, and latency overlap require separate scheduling evidence.

Reproduce and inspect¶

Reproduction requires the original sampled run record, its matching implementation, and a source checkout containing the shared src/openquantum/resource_estimation.py adapter in the pinned Python 3.12/QDK environment. The manifest and signature records identify the executed code, declared model settings, and input hashes. Standalone sampled experiment downloads remain available through the finite-shot chapter; exporting the shared physical adapter is a separate integration step.

The recorded replay concerns only the original four-vertex cycle and first Hamiltonian. The portability cases are different inputs with their own logical records, and do not inherit these physical estimates.

  • Replay manifest and execution contract

  • Every batch and its source/lowered QASM mapping

  • Native canonical/PSSPC model signatures

  • Actual conditional estimator reports

Quality and workload across sizes¶

The earlier examples establish inspectable circuits and small independent checks. This study varies input size and QAOA depth under a fixed sampling protocol, then asks whether the selected states meet stated quality targets. It uses the original QAOA and VQE constructions Farhi et al., 2014Peruzzo et al., 2014; the figures and implementation are original.

Study status and interpretation

The locked recipe has been executed for all 72 runs. Independent post-training audits meet the target in 19 of 60 QAOA runs and 4 of 12 VQE runs. Simultaneous holdout intervals support the target in 18 QAOA runs and no VQE runs; every run supports the separately requested ±0.05\pm0.05±0.05 normalized readout precision. All predetermined runs and misses are retained, with no retuning of initializations, schedule, targets, or readout allocation.

The experiment uses ideal counts drawn classically from circuit probabilities. Simultaneous holdout bounds concern the selected states under that sampling model, not a population success rate, optimizer convergence, physical hardware, or quantum advantage.

Fixed inputs and targets¶

QAOA uses unweighted paths and cycles with n=3,4,5,6,8n=3,4,5,6,8n=3,4,5,6,8 vertices and depths p=1,2p=1,2p=1,2. A path has edges (j,j+1)(j,j+1)(j,j+1); a cycle adds (n−1,0)(n-1,0)(n−1,0). Each depth starts at the interleaved angle vector (0.2,0.1)(0.2,0.1)(0.2,0.1) repeated ppp times, in order (γ0,β0,…)(\gamma_0,\beta_0,\ldots)(γ0​,β0​,…). Three distinct seed namespaces, 7, 19, and 41, give 60 runs across the 20 graph/depth cases.

The minimized training estimate is the negative joint cut mean. All edges are scored from each all-Z bitstring. Full classical enumeration supplies C⋆C_\starC⋆​, independently corroborating the simple references: n−1n-1n−1 for a path, nnn for an even cycle, and n−1n-1n−1 for an odd cycle. The post-training quality target is

⟨C⟩C⋆≥0.80.\frac{\langle C\rangle}{C_\star}\ge0.80.C⋆​⟨C⟩​≥0.80.
(7)

These graph families are classically tractable; the experiment tests implementation behavior and resource growth rather than hard-instance advantage.

VQE uses open chains of n=2,3,4,6n=2,3,4,6n=2,3,4,6 qubits with dimensionless Hamiltonian

Hn=−∑j=0n−1Zj+12∑j=0n−2XjXj+1.H_n=-\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}Z_j +\frac12\sum_{j=0}^{n-2}X_jX_{j+1}.Hn​=−j=0∑n−1​Zj​+21​j=0∑n−2​Xj​Xj+1​.
(8)

Prepare ∣0⟩⊗n|0\rangle^{\otimes n}∣0⟩⊗n, apply one RY(theta[j]) per qubit, and then the ascending CX chain (0,1),(1,2),…,(n−2,n−1)(0,1),(1,2),\ldots,(n-2,n-1)(0,1),(1,2),…,(n−2,n−1). All angles initially equal 0.6. This is a concrete shallow ansatz, not a claim that every chain ground state lies in its circuit family. The three seed namespaces give 12 VQE runs. Dense diagonalization supplies an independent ground-energy reference E0E_0E0​, and the post-training target is energy-density gap

⟨Hn⟩−E0n≤0.05.\frac{\langle H_n\rangle-E_0}{n}\le0.05.n⟨Hn​⟩−E0​​≤0.05.
(9)

Normalization permits a common density target across sizes; it does not fix the same absolute energy tolerance, since the allowed absolute gap is 0.05n0.05n0.05n.

The two diagrams show the final all-Z circuits of the first prescribed case and seed for each method: path n=3,p=1n=3,p=1n=3,p=1 QAOA and chain n=2n=2n=2 VQE, both seed 7. They are selected by recipe order, with every other parameter/basis circuit retained in the manifest. VQE all-X groups additionally apply H to every qubit.

Decisions use sampled objectives¶

Each run makes an initial call with 128 shots per measurement group and then 12 sweeps:

SweepsCoordinate step, radiansShots per group per objective call
1–40.4256
5–80.2512
9–120.11,024

Every sweep freshly samples its incumbent and both coordinate displacements along every parameter, from that same incumbent. The best sampled proposal needs a reduction exceeding twice the combined descriptive standard error. The only stopping rule is schedule exhaustion. This adaptive comparison is a heuristic, not a calibrated test or convergence criterion. Exact selected-state expectations and classical references are kept separate from the sampled quantities used for decisions.

VQE uses two groups. The all-Z score is YZ=−∑jZjY_Z=-\sum_jZ_jYZ​=−∑j​Zj​, with range [−n,n][-n,n][−n,n]. The all-X score is YX=12∑jXjXj+1Y_X=\tfrac12\sum_jX_jX_{j+1}YX​=21​∑j​Xj​Xj+1​ after H basis changes on every qubit, with range [−(n−1)/2,(n−1)/2][-(n-1)/2,(n-1)/2][−(n−1)/2,(n−1)/2]. Each score is formed jointly from one bitstring, preserving covariance among the Z terms and among the overlapping XX terms. The two group means are added; group independence does not make terms within a group independent.

The record retains case definitions, parameter order, every call and proposal, counts, group scores and variance, accepted/rejected moves, and random-stream metadata. Case-specific namespaces distinguish repeated seed labels across inputs, and fresh holdout streams are distinct from training streams NumPy Developers, n.d.. No outcome-based case selection is applied.

Simultaneous holdout precision and selected-state quality¶

After training, all 72 selected states receive a fresh 16,384-shot-per-group holdout. There are 60 QAOA groups and 24 VQE groups, giving 84 predetermined groups. The allocation was chosen analytically before outcomes. Set

δgroup=0.0584,a=log⁡(2/δgroup)2⋅16384≈0.01574146.\delta_{\rm group}=\frac{0.05}{84},\qquad a=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta_{\rm group})}{2\cdot16384}} \approx0.01574146.δgroup​=840.05​,a=2⋅16384log(2/δgroup​)​​≈0.01574146.
(10)

Hoeffding’s inequality and a union bound give simultaneous coverage of all 84 group means with failure probability at most 0.05, under fresh ideal independent samples within each group Hoeffding, 1963. The statement remains conditional on the selected angles and training histories. Between-run independence is not needed for the union bound; valid fresh conditional sampling for each group is needed.

The recorded QAOA group uses the conservative input edge-count range [0,m][0,m][0,m], so its ratio radius is (m/C⋆)a(m/C_\star)a(m/C⋆​)a. The enumerated C⋆C_\starC⋆​ normalizes the post-training report; it does not enter sampled optimization decisions. For VQE, adding the two group intervals and dividing by nnn gives energy-density radius

ϵdensity=(3−1/n)a.\epsilon_{\rm density}=(3-1/n)a.ϵdensity​=(3−1/n)a.
(11)

It ranges from about 0.03935 at n=2n=2n=2 to 0.04460 at n=6n=6n=6. These radii support the separately declared simultaneous ±0.05\pm0.05±0.05 readout-precision allocation. This does not imply that every selected state achieves the optimization target.

The result table therefore separates three statements: post-training exact audit meets the target; the simultaneous holdout interval supports that selected-state target; and the measurement allocation supports the requested expectation precision. Sampled support requires a QAOA lower ratio endpoint at least 0.80, or a VQE upper density-gap endpoint at most 0.05. An interval crossing the target is inconclusive; lack of support is not itself proof of a target miss. Raw estimates and interval endpoints remain visible even if shot noise gives a negative energy-density gap. A negative lower endpoint does not establish energy below the ground state.

This frozen, bounded study retains every predetermined run and every target miss. It covers 60 QAOA runs on path/cycle graphs with n = 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 and p = 1, 2, plus 12 VQE runs on n = 2, 3, 4, 6 chains. Each case uses seeds 7, 19 and 41 with the same initialization. QAOA angles start at interleaved (0.2, 0.1) per layer. VQE uses H = -sum Z + 0.5 sum nearest-neighbor XX, one layer of n RY gates followed by a CX chain, and all initial angles 0.6.

Training uses raw sampled cut or energy scores. Exact classical optima/eigenvalues are post-run references, never optimizer decisions. The fixed schedule has four sweeps each at (step radians, shots/group) = (0.4, 256), (0.2, 512), (0.1, 1024), with 128 shots/group for the initial call. Every sweep remeasures the incumbent and both displacements of every coordinate. The two-standard-error acceptance margin remains a heuristic without a convergence guarantee.

Fresh holdouts use 16,384 shots per measurement group. Their pointwise per-run bounds are reported separately from the whole-study allocation δ = 0.05 across 84 holdout groups. The resulting group intervals combine into conditional fixed-state ratio/energy-density intervals. A ±0.05 expectation precision bound is distinct from reaching a quality target. The audited quality targets are QAOA mean cut / classical optimum ≥0.80 and VQE energy-density gap ≤0.05.

The record contains 6,408 sampled objective calls, 7,656 group batches, and 5,859,840 modeled circuit preparations (4,483,584 training and 1,376,256 fresh holdout shots). All counts are classically sampled from ideal circuit probabilities; no QPU execution or noise is measured. The source manifest links every group’s parameters, basis, RNG stream, shots, exact OpenQASM hash, depth and logical gate counts. Byte-identical source circuits share a file only after SHA-256 comparison.

The p=2 QAOA runs use more coordinates, proposals and shots than p=1 under this fixed sweep schedule. Their different costs are explicit; this is not an equal-budget comparison. Circuit loading/preparation, basis changes and every rejected/accepted evaluation are included in the source ledger. Rotations are unsynthesized, routing/reset/device latency are unmeasured, and no physical-resource comparison is inferred. CPU timings measure the simulator and classical control, not quantum hardware time.

The achieved quality depends on the tested input and recipe. Paths at n=3n=3n=3 meet the target in all six depth/seed runs; among the larger paths, only the n=4,p=2n=4,p=2n=4,p=2, seed 41 run meets it. The odd cycles at n=3,5n=3,5n=3,5 meet the target in all twelve runs, while every tested even-cycle run misses it. Odd cycles have C⋆=n−1C_\star=n-1C⋆​=n−1, so their ratio denominator differs from that of an even cycle; these results do not imply a monotone size trend.

The VQE density gap is 0.010811–0.011081 at n=2n=2n=2, and 0.179165–0.235975 at n=6n=6n=6. The recorded zero-state baseline at n=6n=6n=6 has density gap 0.0525804, so the three fitted six-spin states also miss that simple baseline. The fixed search is retained rather than restarted from a more favorable point. Its four exact target hits remain distinct from the zero simultaneous holdout supports: a valid expectation-precision allocation can still leave a quality threshold inconclusive.

All target misses remain visible. They can reflect the circuit family, initialization, finite search budget, and sampled decisions. One limitation is already known independently: the depth-one C4 formula in the main chapter has maximum mean three, hence ratio 3/43/43/4, below this study’s 0.80 target. A perfect angle optimizer cannot make that circuit family meet the target. The study does not identify the cause of every other miss or estimate a general success probability.

At depth two, more parameters cause more calls and shots, and each circuit also has more layers. A quality improvement at p=2p=2p=2 would therefore be observed under a larger workload, not an equal-budget comparison. Larger VQE inputs likewise increase the proposal count and per-shot circuit width.

Before compilation, one QAOA preparation uses nnn H, npnpnp RX, mpmpmp RZ, and 2mp2mp2mp CX. The stated VQE ansatz uses nnn RY and n−1n-1n−1 CX; its all-X group adds nnn H, and every group measures nnn qubits. Source gates must be weighted by every recorded group’s shots. CPU simulation/control times, reference calculation, and postprocessing are separate from hypothetical quantum gate/measurement time. The recorded numerical workflow took 4.704195 s of CPU-host wall time and 4.701387 s of process CPU time; trace export and plotting are outside those study timers. Neither time measures hardware feedback. Statevectors and dense references still grow exponentially; this bounded study is not an asymptotic performance test.

Conditional physical replay and verification limits¶

Physical projection concerns the complete frozen recorded workloads, rather than one final ansatz. The replay fixes stored parameters, measurement groups, and shot weights. Fresh hardware outcomes could lead to another adaptive trajectory and another resource cost. These are costs of replaying the protocol, not certified costs of attaining its targets. A lower-cost run that misses quality cannot establish an improvement at matched requested quality.

The physical layer now reports a computed conditional replay of all 72 recorded runs. It covers all 5,859,840 preparations and 84 model cost classes. The original 64-search guard stopped before any physical-estimator search, and that complete pending result remains in the cap-64 archive. A recorded computation-only amendment raised the search limit to 96 before new searches, without changing cases, seeds, targets, shots, hardware profiles, or error allowances. The amended plan completed 85 physical-estimator searches, including the distinct-QASM cost-consistency probe. Profiles remain frozen at physical error 10-3 or 10-4, with 100 ns gates and 500 ns measurements.

Reproduce and inspect¶

Use the pinned Python 3.12 environment and original package credits in the main chapter. The recipe, all runs, resource ledger, objective-call CSV, group CSV, and all final qualities and intervals expose the complete experiment.

The circuit manifest maps the exact QASM hashes to cases, parameters, groups, and repetition counts. Standalone implementation, generator, and MIT license accompany the executed verification notebook. The notebook loads matching runs.json and module snapshots, checks their hashes, and independently replays the recorded decisions and references without repeating training. For standalone execution, save both runs.json and optimization.py beside the notebook and use the pinned environment.

python scripts/verify_optimization_checkpoint.py
python -m pytest tests/test_optimization_quality_scaling.py tests/test_optimization_scaling_vqe.py
python scripts/generate_optimization_quality_resources.py --max-queries 96 --max-wall-seconds 1200 --require-complete

The resource driver requires the audited shared source-checkout adapter. Its source and MIT license are available for inspection; it supplies no actual synthesized angle sequences or reset model.

The generator preserves the numerical checkpoint and refuses to overwrite an existing study with a fresh run. --resume completes exports from matching snapshots; a new numerical reproduction needs a separate output directory. The raw checkpoint supports that recorded-workflow replay.

Saved notebook outputs serve the static site without a public kernel. Larger generators, alternative schedules, and any physical adaptive experiment require separate records and validation.

Initialization and sampling diagnostics¶

The quality-and-workload study retained many target misses under its fixed sampling schedule. Those results leave several possible explanations: an unreachable target in the circuit family, an unfavorable initialization, a limited search, or sampled decisions. This diagnostic study fixes two starts and equal training preparation counts for a smaller set of inputs. It uses the same original QAOA and VQE constructions Farhi et al., 2014Peruzzo et al., 2014; the implementation and figures are original.

Study status and interpretation

The frozen numerical recipe has executed all 36 sampled runs and 24 separately labeled deterministic CPU controls. Independent post-training audits meet the target in 4 of 24 QAOA runs and 2 of 12 VQE runs. Simultaneous holdout intervals support the target in three QAOA runs and no VQE runs; all 36 runs support the separately requested ±0.05\pm0.05±0.05 normalized readout precision. Every prescribed run and miss remains in the record.

Counts are generated classically from ideal circuit probabilities; no QPU or calibrated hardware noise is measured. The earlier 72-run study, its misses, source records, and conditional physical replay remain unchanged.

Equal training preparation counts do not imply equal objective calls, measured qubits, source gates, synthesis, physical qubits, or runtime. These bounded ideal numerical diagnostics cannot establish calibrated hardware-noise behavior, general optimizer convergence, or quantum advantage.

Fixed cases, starts, and targets¶

QAOA uses the unweighted cycles C4 and C6, each at depths p=1,2p=1,2p=1,2. For nnn vertices the cycle edges are (j,j+1)(j,j+1)(j,j+1) for j=0,…,n−2j=0,\ldots,n-2j=0,…,n−2, together with (n−1,0)(n-1,0)(n−1,0). Each run minimizes the negative joint cut mean. The two predetermined starts, in interleaved (γ0,β0,…)(\gamma_0,\beta_0,\ldots)(γ0​,β0​,…) order, repeat either (0.2,0.1)(0.2,0.1)(0.2,0.1) or (0.6,0.4)(0.6,0.4)(0.6,0.4) in every layer.

VQE uses open chains of n=4,6n=4,6n=4,6 qubits with dimensionless Hamiltonian

Hn=−∑j=0n−1Zj+12∑j=0n−2XjXj+1.H_n=-\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}Z_j +\frac12\sum_{j=0}^{n-2}X_jX_{j+1}.Hn​=−j=0∑n−1​Zj​+21​j=0∑n−2​Xj​Xj+1​.
(12)

Prepare ∣0⟩⊗n|0\rangle^{\otimes n}∣0⟩⊗n, apply RY(theta[j]) to each qubit, and then the ascending CX chain (0,1),(1,2),…,(n−2,n−1)(0,1),(1,2),\ldots,(n-2,n-1)(0,1),(1,2),…,(n−2,n−1). The two starts set every angle to 0.6 or every angle to zero. They are prescribed before sampling; diagnostic witnesses and angles selected by the earlier study never initialize these runs.

The six cases, two starts, and seed labels 7, 19, and 41 give 36 sampled runs. Distinct case/start namespaces and separate training/holdout streams distinguish repeated seed labels NumPy Developers, n.d.. Every prescribed run and every failed or inconclusive outcome is retained.

The quality targets preserve those of the earlier study:

QAOA: ⟨C⟩C⋆≥0.80,VQE: ⟨Hn⟩−E0n≤0.05.\text{QAOA: }\frac{\langle C\rangle}{C_\star}\ge0.80, \qquad \text{VQE: }\frac{\langle H_n\rangle-E_0}{n}\le0.05.QAOA: C⋆​⟨C⟩​≥0.80,VQE: n⟨Hn​⟩−E0​​≤0.05.
(13)

Classical enumeration supplies C⋆=nC_\star=nC⋆​=n for these even cycles, and independent dense diagonalization supplies E0E_0E0​. The references normalize post-training quality; they do not supply sampled optimization decisions. The density tolerance is an absolute energy tolerance of 0.05n0.05n0.05n, so it varies with nnn.

Each sweep freshly evaluates its incumbent and both displacements along every coordinate from that incumbent. Polling visits coordinates in ascending order, minus then plus. It chooses the smallest estimated proposal objective and accepts only when

f^incumbent−f^proposal>2SE^incumbent 2+SE^proposal 2.\widehat f_{\rm incumbent}-\widehat f_{\rm proposal} >2\sqrt{\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}_{\rm incumbent}^{\,2} +\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}_{\rm proposal}^{\,2}}.f​incumbent​−f​proposal​>2SEincumbent2​+SEproposal2​​.
(15)

Angles wrap to [−π,π)[-\pi,\pi)[−π,π). The schedule is exhausted without an outcome-based stopping rule. Choosing among proposals and adapting the angles makes this two-standard-error margin a descriptive heuristic, not a calibrated hypothesis test or convergence certificate.

For QAOA, each all-Z bitstring jointly scores every cut edge. VQE has an all-Z score YZ=−∑jZjY_Z=-\sum_jZ_jYZ​=−∑j​Zj​ and an all-X score YX=12∑jXjXj+1Y_X=\tfrac12\sum_jX_jX_{j+1}YX​=21​∑j​Xj​Xj+1​, after H basis changes on all qubits. Joint bitstring scores retain covariance among terms within each group. The two group means add to the energy, with independent fresh samples between groups.

The sampled optimizer uses only these counts, estimated objectives, and descriptive errors. Exact expectations of selected states are post-training audits. The record must retain every incumbent, proposal, count batch, margin, and rejection, so an observed success cannot hide the effort or failures preceding it.

One obstruction is known independently of the search. For both tested depth-one cycles, conjugating each edge observable through the mixer and cost layer gives mean cut contribution 1/2+sin⁡(4β)sin⁡(2γ)/41/2+\sin(4\beta)\sin(2\gamma)/41/2+sin(4β)sin(2γ)/4. Summing the nnn edges gives

⟨C⟩=n2+n4sin⁡(4β)sin⁡(2γ),n∈{4,6}.\langle C\rangle=\frac n2+\frac n4\sin(4\beta)\sin(2\gamma), \qquad n\in\{4,6\}.⟨C⟩=2n​+4n​sin(4β)sin(2γ),n∈{4,6}.
(16)

Since both sine factors are bounded by one, its maximum ratio is 3/43/43/4, attained at γ=π/4,β=π/8\gamma=\pi/4,\beta=\pi/8γ=π/4,β=π/8 and below the preserved 0.80 target. These angles are an explanatory analytic anchor, never a sampled or control start. More shots or a perfect angle optimizer cannot lift that circuit-family ceiling. Deterministic angle checks corroborate the formula rather than prove a universal bound; the bound follows from the expression itself. This circuit limit is separate from an unsuccessful local search, and deterministic controls do not themselves prove infeasibility for other cases.

Two deterministic CPU controls¶

For each of the twelve case/start pairs, two deterministic controls follow the same coordinate order, step schedule, and strict acceptance rule. They have no seed replication because no random outcomes are drawn.

For the second mode, if YgY_gYg​ is a group score and sgs_gsg​ is its virtual allocation, the squared effective error is ∑gVar⁡(Yg)/sg\sum_g\operatorname{Var}(Y_g)/s_g∑g​Var(Yg​)/sg​. It evaluates the acceptance margin at exact means. It is not the expectation of the noisy adaptive path: sampling can change the winning proposal, its estimated error, and every later angle.

Both controls consume zero quantum preparations. Their virtual sampling allocations define a CPU diagnostic margin; they are never counted as actual QPU shots or treated as free quantum expectations. Circuit expectations, population moments, and independent references are classically calculated on the bounded inputs. Their CPU times and virtual budgets must remain separate from the sampled workload and physical source metadata.

A difference between starts shows behavior of this prescribed search on these cases. A difference between the exact objective and expected margin controls helps expose the effect of the acceptance rule. A difference between either control and sampled runs includes selection and adaptive-path effects; it does not identify a calibrated hardware-noise law or isolate a unique cause for every miss.

Fresh holdout precision and selected-state quality¶

Every sampled selected state receives a fresh 16,384-shot-per-group holdout. There are 24 QAOA final groups and 24 VQE final groups, so the family has 48 predetermined groups. Allocate

δgroup=0.0548,a=log⁡(2/δgroup)2⋅16,384.\delta_{\rm group}=\frac{0.05}{48},\qquad a=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta_{\rm group})}{2\cdot16{,}384}}.δgroup​=480.05​,a=2⋅16,384log(2/δgroup​)​​.
(17)

Hoeffding’s inequality and a union bound provide simultaneous coverage of those 48 group means with failure probability at most 0.05, conditional on the selected states and training histories under fresh ideal independent samples within each group Hoeffding, 1963. The union bound does not require independence between runs. It does require valid fresh conditional sampling for every group.

The conservative QAOA score range [0,m][0,m][0,m] gives ratio radius (m/C⋆)a=a(m/C_\star)a=a(m/C⋆​)a=a for these even cycles. The VQE group ranges [−n,n][-n,n][−n,n] and [−(n−1)/2,(n−1)/2][-(n-1)/2,(n-1)/2][−(n−1)/2,(n−1)/2] give energy-density radius (3−1/n)a(3-1/n)a(3−1/n)a. These radii assess the separately requested simultaneous ±0.05\pm0.05±0.05 expectation precision.

Selected-state quality is a separate statement. A QAOA lower ratio endpoint at least 0.80 supports the target, while an upper endpoint below 0.80 supports a miss. A VQE upper density-gap endpoint at most 0.05 supports the target, while a lower endpoint above 0.05 supports a miss. An interval crossing the threshold is inconclusive. Raw means and endpoints remain visible, including negative sampled energy-density gaps; shot noise cannot establish an expectation below the ground energy.

The final report therefore distinguishes exact target hits, holdout-supported targets, holdout-supported misses, inconclusive intervals, and expectation precision. Deterministic controls have no sampled holdout confidence claim.

Recorded outcomes and what they distinguish¶

The frozen study retains all 36 sampled trajectories: C4/C6 QAOA at p = 1, 2 and open-chain VQE at n = 4, 6, with two fixed starts and seeds 7, 19, 41. No fifth-increment winning angles or analytic witnesses initialize a run. Each sampled run has exactly 65,648 training preparations, then 16,384 fresh shots per measurement group. All accepted and rejected candidates remain in the trace.

The 24 deterministic CPU controls use the same 12 case/start combinations and fixed polling schedule. Exact-objective controls set the comparison standard error to zero. Expected-margin controls use exact means and true population variances divided by the prescribed virtual group allocation. These controls contain no random counts and use zero actual quantum preparations; their allocations are prospective bookkeeping.

QAOA quality means mean cut divided by the enumerated optimum (target ≥0.80). VQE quality means energy-density gap above the dense ground energy (target ≤0.05). Fresh holdout bounds allocate total failure 0.05 across all 48 final groups, conditional on fixed trained parameters. The accepted-move margin is a heuristic; these finite controls do not certify the global ansatz optimum, population optimizer-success probability or convergence.

Actual ideal-sampled workload: 3,672 objective calls, 5,280 measured groups, 3,149,760 preparations. The deterministic controls record 2,424 exact CPU oracle evaluations with zero actual measured groups/preparations. Counts are simulated from ideal probabilities; no QPU or hardware noise was measured. Actual source costs include 82,488,288 shot-weighted unitary gates and 15,748,800 qubit readouts.

Input/state preparation gates, measurement-basis changes, every proposed circuit and all final readout shots are included in the actual source/readout ledger. Equal preparation budgets do not imply equal gate or physical cost. Rotations remain unsynthesized; physical initialization/reset, routing, communication and feedback time are unmeasured, and no physical projection or hardware advantage is inferred. All CPU timings, exact-QASM exports and producer snapshots are recorded separately. Existing Lean coverage remains classical C4 reference coverage only.

All twelve depth-one QAOA runs miss the target, as required by the analytic circuit ceiling above. At C4 depth two, all three runs from the alternative start reach ratio 0.988199, with simultaneous holdout support, while none from the original start reaches 0.80. Both deterministic controls show the same start contrast. This is behavior of these two prescribed starts on one case, not an estimated population success probability.

The C6 depth-two results differ. The original start has one exact target hit, seed 19, at ratio 0.805210; its holdout interval crosses 0.80 and is inconclusive. All three alternative-start sampled runs miss the exact target. For that alternative start, the exact objective control reaches 0.830926 after eight accepted moves, while the expected margin control reaches 0.794687 after two. The successful exact control supplies a state in this circuit family above the target, and the margin changes this fixed search path. Neither fact predicts what another sampled trajectory will select.

For four-spin VQE, the zero start gives two sampled exact target hits, seeds 7 and 41, at density gap 0.037892; seed 19 ends at 0.050844 and misses. All three holdout intervals are inconclusive. The zero state’s exact density gap is already 0.047100: its expected margin control accepts no move, while its exact objective control reaches 0.032233. From the original all-0.6 start, the sampled gaps are 0.123778–0.229939, all with holdout-supported misses. Its exact objective control also reaches 0.032233, but its expected margin control accepts no move and stays at 0.564205.

Every six-spin sampled run misses the target. The original-start gaps are 0.498964–0.596566, with holdout-supported misses. The zero-start gaps are 0.052580–0.055903, with inconclusive holdouts; two sampled trajectories worsen the zero-state baseline, and seed 41 stays at it. From zero, the exact objective control reaches 0.042669 and meets the target, while the expected margin control accepts no move and retains the baseline 0.052580. The exact controls thus exhibit target-reaching states for both VQE inputs without claiming that either ansatz contains its full ground state. The failed original-start six-spin exact control, at gap 0.087448, is a local-search outcome rather than an infeasibility result.

Across the 36 sampled final states, holdouts support three targets, 24 misses, and leave nine inconclusive. All 36 support the separate expectation-precision allocation. The figure below retains accepted-move counts for every sampled seed and both deterministic modes. Accepted moves need not improve the exact objective when their decisions use sampled counts, and a control with no accepted moves still consumes its full CPU evaluation schedule.

Complete workload and physical limits¶

The executed 36-run sampled allocation has 2,363,328 training preparations and 786,432 holdout preparations, for 3,149,760 total modeled preparations. It makes 3,672 sampled objective calls, including final validation, and 5,280 measured group batches. These counts include initial calls, fresh incumbents, every rejected and accepted proposal, and final readout; the executed record reconciles with the fixed allocation.

Equal training counts leave important workload differences. A QAOA preparation uses nnn H, npnpnp RX, mpmpmp RZ, and 2mp2mp2mp CX source gates. A VQE preparation uses nnn RY and n−1n-1n−1 CX; its all-X group adds nnn H. Each group measures all nnn qubits. The complete source ledger weights every recorded parameter/basis circuit by its group’s shots, including the full trajectory and final readout. The VQE holdout also uses two groups per selected state, so equal training counts do not give equal full readout workloads.

The executed source ledger records 82,488,288 shot-weighted unitary gates, 15,748,800 individual qubit readouts, and peak width six. The circuit manifest maps all 5,280 sampled group batches to 1,147 unique source-QASM exports, parameters, bases, hashes, and shot weights. Deduplicating an export does not remove any repetitions from the ledger.

The input is an explicitly generated graph or the stated local Hamiltonian. QAOA objective phases, initial H or RY preparation, CX chains, VQE basis changes, repetitions, and readout belong to the source workload. Dense references, statevectors, population moments, sampling, and controller wall/CPU times are classical costs recorded separately.

Circuit generation and simulation have separate limits. The source generators cap materialization at 100,000 unitary gates per circuit, and the chain-VQE generator supports 2–32 qubits. The sampled and dense-reference routines cap inputs at eight qubits; this study uses at most six. These four- and six-qubit controls do not remove the exponential cost of generic statevector simulation or dense reference calculations.

The deterministic controls make 2,424 exact CPU objective evaluations, plus 24 independent final audits, with zero quantum preparations or measured groups. Their virtual training allocations are excluded from the sampled ledger. The numerical timing record reports 3.855905 s of CPU-host wall time and 3.773667 s of process CPU time, including numerical checks and checkpoint writes. Trace reconstruction, export, and plotting have separate timings in the full run record. None of these times measures quantum hardware or physical feedback.

This study has no new physical projection. Arbitrary source rotations remain unsynthesized. Physical initialization/reset, routing, transport, communication, device latency, and adaptive hardware feedback are unmeasured, and no common physical configuration is verified. The earlier conditional physical replay remains a separate frozen record, rather than a physical-cost proxy for this new recipe. A quality miss cannot establish an improvement at matched successful output quality.

Bounded verification and reproducibility¶

The generator reconciles all 36 sampled histories with the fixed starts, schedules, namespaces, group allocations, and recorded decision rule. Counts replay the sampled decisions without exact means, while independent cut enumeration, circuit expectations, dense ground energies, and joint score moments audit final quality and control definitions. All 24 control paths retain their proposals and rejections as well.

The recipe, raw numerical checkpoint, full runs, sampled objectives, measured groups, and final qualities and intervals expose the sampled calculation. The control results and every control evaluation keep exact means, population variances, virtual allocations, and effective decision margins visible.

Matching standalone implementation, generator, environment lock, and MIT license accompany the executed verification notebook. The notebook checks matching hashes and replays saved sampled decisions, controls, references, holdouts, and workloads without repeating training. For standalone execution, copy the complete diagnostics artifact directory, place the notebook inside it, and run there using the pinned environment. The audit requires the matching implementation and generator snapshots, runs.json, resources.json, circuit-manifest.json, and its circuits/ QASM files.

From the source checkout:

python -m pytest tests/test_optimization_diagnostics.py
python scripts/generate_optimization_diagnostics.py --resume

The generator’s --resume mode preserves the frozen numerical checkpoint and matching producer bytes while completing verification or exports. It refuses a changed recipe or producer. Standalone resume additionally requires the complete saved artifact directory, including freeze.json, recipe.json, raw-study.json, numerical-timing.json, every file under checkpoints/, the license, and the environment lock. From that copied directory, run python generate_optimization_diagnostics.py --output-dir . --resume. A fresh numerical reproduction requires a separate output directory, a preserved recipe/producer freeze, and the same bounded execution checks.

Use the pinned Python 3.12 environment and exact package credits in the main chapter. Saved notebook outputs serve the static site without a public kernel. Larger inputs, alternative starts or schedules, calibrated hardware sampling, and physical adaptive execution require new records and validation.

Classical C4 reference coverage only. The existing Lean artifact does not prove these QAOA circuits, VQE ansätze, stochastic searches, deterministic controls, simultaneous intervals, or resource models.

Verification and formalization¶

The saved audits check explicit source and lowered circuits, original measurement maps, recorded sampled decisions, fresh holdout allocations and complete repetition ledgers. The three recipes retain different inputs, schedules and confidence families. Their simultaneous selected-state intervals do not certify training convergence, a fresh adaptive hardware path or calibrated physical error.

Classical C4 reference coverage only. The existing reproduced Lean artifact covers finite cut values and the stated classical equality predicate. It does not prove the QAOA or VQE circuits, stochastic or deterministic search paths, simultaneous intervals, rotation synthesis or physical resource models. The proof source and verification record retain that exact coverage.
